sources.title: Official GEMS problem description and submission format
sources.verified_claim: Fault location is the target, not confirmed geothermal vents. DTI uses alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, triangular 300 m kernel. GeoTIFF: one float32 band, EPSG:32611, 100 m grid, matching bounds, confidence [0,1]; text says null/NaN outside bounds.
sources.limits: Both chunks read via fetch_page. Not an authenticated download, portal test, or private scorer audit. Zeros outside the irregular footprint are a compatibility variant, not a guarantee of official acceptance.

sources.title: DOE/NLR September 2026 Official Rules, sections 3.2–3.5
sources.verified_claim: Three submissions per week stated in sections 3.2 and 3.4; one final submission across both rounds. AI use is allowed with disclosure in narrative. Finalists deliver reproducible code/assets/documentation; eligibility applies.
sources.limits: All seven extracted chunks read. Current account-specific allowance, rules acceptance and eligibility not accessed or established. This is not a submission receipt.

sources.limits: First page chunk observed 2026-10-25 via research fetch tool, not a submission-page receipt. Does not identify the owner, local raster, private performance or future leaderboard state. No recurring DrivenData monitoring added.

sources.title: USGS GeoDAWN release description
sources.verified_claim: Glen and Earney 2024 release, DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ, CC0. Magnetic data constrain subsurface structure; radiometrics surface geology/soil. Area 2 nominal flight-line spacing is 400 m and flight height varies with terrain; processed grid products include GeoTIFFs.
sources.limits: Both page chunks read. Listing/license verified; original binary grids and processing histories not independently re-downloaded. A magnetic contact does not prove slip or a geothermal vent.

sources.title: DOE GDR INGENIOUS regional compilation 1391
sources.verified_claim: DOI 10.15121/1881483; publicly accessible, CC BY 4.0; lists faults, shear/dilation, magnetics/gravity, heat flow, MT, paleogeothermal features, well/spring chemistry and probe resources with official resource links.
sources.limits: Resource listing/citation portion read. Listing obtainable does not mean binary bytes, schema, footprint coverage or local mirror transformation authenticated.

sources.title: DrivenData official reference solution
sources.verified_claim: Official notebook implements U-Net with Monte Carlo patch splits and TverskyLoss alpha=0.2 beta=0.8. README supports CPU-only environments as well as GPU acceleration.
sources.limits: README and notebook fetched at pinned GitHub commit; notebook does not establish this repository's buffered whole-system validation or certify its results.

sources.title: Grauch & Cordell (1987), HG contact-location limitations
sources.verified_claim: HG maxima can be offset when contacts are not near vertical or when sources are close together. DOI 10.1190/1.1442236.
sources.limits: Official USGS publication abstract read in full. Supports ambiguity, not S18 linear-in-height extrapolation or verified fault displacement.

sources.title: USGS pymaxspots software release (2025)
sources.verified_claim: HG maxspots mark edges of contrasts associated with faults, intrusions OR lithologic contacts. DOI 10.5066/P13FSKEM; source page marks CC0.
sources.limits: Software description and citation read. Software not installed/used; no claim it validates S18 candidates.

sources.title: USGS OFR 02-98, Phillips: aeromagnetic processing and interpretation
sources.verified_claim: HG contact interpretation assumes vertical field/magnetizations, vertical isolated thick sources; violations shift peaks or add secondary peaks. Reduction to the pole is usually needed.
sources.limits: Introduction/flight-line noise/HG assumptions portion read, not all five extracted chunks. S18 used raw TMI; these limitations are a caution, not a tuned correction.

sources.title: Hermant et al. 2025, Stanford geothermal workshop paper
sources.verified_claim: Figure 2 states USGS/TLS fault-label offsets can reach 400 m; introduction notes faults can be permeability conduits or barriers.
sources.limits: Abstract, introduction and Figure 2 chunk read; not all eight chunks. Conference paper, not official competition truth or validation of the new heuristic.
